topic: Diagnosing causation claims and biased study designs

traps.desc: quoted the doubling as the share, reporting a 100 percent figure instead of the fraction of total sales

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response must say that a rise from 4 to 8 units is indeed a doubling, but out of 5000 total sales it is a change from 0.08 percent to 0.16 percent of the market; the percentage change is large only because the starting number is tiny, so the headline is misleading without the base figure. Full credit requires naming the small base as the reason.

traps.desc: divided by the whole membership instead of by the number who actually responded

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response must say that the 240 people who answered chose to answer -- a voluntary response sample -- and that members with strong feelings are far likelier to reply than the 2760 who stayed silent, so the seven-eighths figure describes the respondents only and cannot be extended to the whole membership. Full credit requires naming voluntary response, self-selection or nonresponse bias.
problems.slot: (b) why it cannot be reported for all members

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response must say that the strong association is produced by a third variable, hot weather, which independently raises both ice cream sales and the number of people swimming; neither variable acts on the other, so no amount of correlation supports the causal claim. Full credit requires naming a plausible common cause.
problems.slot: (b) name the flaw in the causal claim

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response must say that people leaving a gym are not representative of the town, because being at a gym is itself evidence of exercising; this is a convenience sample drawn from exactly the group most likely to answer yes, so the three-quarters figure is biased upward. Full credit requires naming the convenience or undercoverage bias and the direction of the bias.
problems.slot: (b) name the bias and its direction

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response must say that the students chose for themselves whether to take the course, so the two groups may already have differed in motivation, prior achievement or family resources; those confounding variables offer an alternative explanation for the 8-point gap, and only random assignment to the course would rule them out. Full credit requires naming self-selection or confounding and proposing random assignment.
problems.slot: (c) why the gap does not show the course works

traps.desc: reported the relative reduction as if it were the absolute change in risk

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response must distinguish the relative reduction, which really is 50 percent, from the absolute reduction of 1 case in 1000, and say that the headline quotes the larger-sounding relative figure while the number of people actually helped is one in a thousand. Full credit requires both figures named and the point that the relative figure alone hides the base rate.

problems.slot: (a) the proportion that thrived when treated

traps.desc: used all 400 plants as the denominator instead of the 200 that were treated

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct response must say that the treated plants all sat on the sunny half of the field, so sunlight is confounded with the fertilizer and either could explain the higher survival; the fix is to assign the treatment at random across the whole field, or at least to block by sun exposure so both treatments appear in each part. Full credit requires naming the confounding and proposing randomization or blocking.
problems.slot: (b) name the design flaw and the fix

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response must say that flu-shot campaigns and hospital admissions both peak in winter because the season drives them, so the winter itself is the common cause and the timing is no evidence that the shots cause admissions; the response must also note that the direction could even be reversed, since people who feel at risk seek both, and must name a randomized trial comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated groups as the evidence that would settle it.
